subject: Defining success: Snyder Health MAP — acceptance guardrails & exit tests
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Snyder <jessica.snyder@snyderhealth.com>, Marc Williams <marc.williams@procure-snyder.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Defining success: Snyder Health MAP — acceptance guardrails & exit tests

Hi Jessica / Marc,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on the goal: a short trial that proves we can meet 95th percentile latency and maintain >=92% semantic accuracy on your triage intent set. To make the MAP actionable for both sides, I sketched a compact acceptance blueprint (attached) and suggested exit gates. High level:

- Objective: Demonstrate production-grade inference for triage use (live traffic sandbox).
- Timebox: 4-week evaluation start -> end (pilot window: Sep 1 — Sep 28).
- Key SLOs: 95th pctl latency <= 450ms, inference cost target <= $0.018/token, intent classification F1 >= 0.92 measured on labeled probe set.
- Exit gates (must be satisfied to close):
  1) Performance: 95th pctl latency under SLO for three consecutive days at representative load.
  2) Quality: Pass rate >= 92% on weekly labeled probe set; no single critical misclassification in production-simulated traffic.
  3) Ops: Rollback and fallback configured; alerting integrated into Snyder PagerDuty.
  4) Security & compliance: Scoped VPC connectivity verified; retention policy aligned with Snyder's 90-day requirement.

Please see the attached "snyder-map-draft-v1.pdf" for a proposed week-by-week checklist and the CSV with suggested acceptance tests.

Next steps for us:
- You: confirm stakeholder list and whether the labeled probe set below represents final scope (I used the samples you shared).
- Us: finalize test harness and provision the sandbox env with RBAC and telemetry.

Would Tuesday next week (Aug 12, 11am PT) work for a short alignment call to finalize the MAP and signoffs?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: snyder-map-draft-v1.pdf (proposal), acceptance-test-catalog.csv (probe tests)

From: Jessica Snyder <jessica.snyder@snyderhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marc Williams <marc.williams@procure-snyder.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Defining success: Snyder Health MAP — acceptance guardrails & exit tests

Kimberly — thanks, this is exactly the clarity we needed. A few quick notes:

- Timeline: Sep 1 start is OK but can we shift to Sep 3 (internal change freeze Sep 2).
- Quality metric: 92% F1 is acceptable as the primary signal; can we add a secondary check for false positives on emergent-category 'urgent_followup' (we've seen high cost if we overtriage).
- Ops: Confirmed — security will need the VPC diagram; can you include expected egress patterns?

I'll loop in our security lead (cc'd Marc) to the alignment call. Tuesday at 11am PT works for us.

—Jessica
Director, Digital Intake | Snyder Health
jessica.snyder@snyderhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Snyder <jessica.snyder@snyderhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Aug 2025 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Defining success: Snyder Health MAP — acceptance guardrails & exit tests

Jessica / Kimberly — adding the fed-back items into the acceptance-test-catalog. Notes on implementation:

- "urgent_followup" FP rate check: we'll add an automated weekly confusion matrix and a targeted adversarial probe for that label.
- VPC/egress: I'll attach a one-page network pattern diagram to the shared Drive link and paste a short summary below in the call: expected egress is to our metrics collectors (TLS to telemetry.redwood.ai) + occasional model artifact pulls from S3-like storage; all outbound over port 443 only.
- Cost target: the $0.018/token assumes q4-24 small-batch path; if throughput or seq length increases we'll surface recommendation flags in the dashboard.

I'll prepare the sandbox with a canary route and the probe injection harness prior to Sep 3.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: (draft network-patterns.pdf uploaded to shared Drive)

On Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 11:00 AM PDT Jessica Snyder <jessica.snyder@snyderhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks, team — good alignment. Two quick action items: can the acceptance tests include a smoke scenario that mimics Monday morning peak (10am local) with a short 30-minute burst at 2x nominal traffic? Also please include an explicit rollback play for the false-positive spike case.

Replying inline with owners and next steps: 
- Ben: can you add the Monday-peak smoke scenario and the FP spike rollback runbook to the CSV by EOD Wed (Aug 13)?
- Karthik: I'll need a short doc on the canary routing policy and the auto-fallback to the smaller base model for cost/reliability; can you draft by Aug 14?
- Jessica / Marc: once Ben & Karthik confirm, we'll circulate a 1-page MAP signoff and a short mutual action timeline for approvals.

Closing note — once the three exit gates (performance, quality, ops) are satisfied for the test window, we'll propose a staged handoff to your Platform team with 30-day runbook overlap.

Thanks all,
Kimberly
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
